events.text:
## Recommendation
- **Go to Grand Haven.** It has the newest boat report, so it's the best guide to this week.
- **Ratings for this week (boat salmon, 0-4):** Grand Haven 2, South Haven 2, Muskegon 2, St. Joseph 2. Each rating is a judgment from reports that are 1 to 3 weeks old, so none is a confident call.
- **Run lines 35-100 ft down in 60-120 ft of water** off Grand Haven, with green and orange spoons and white flasher flies.
- **Backup: St. Joseph,** if you can get a cold-water drop. Its July 10 boat report was excellent on spoons at 80-90 ft of water.

## Why
- Grand Haven has the newest boat report (July 24), and it's the only one from this past week. It describes Chinook, with a few coho, at 35-100 ft down in 60-120 ft of water on spoons and flashers.
- The July 24 Grand Haven report rated coho only 1 and left the Chinook unrated, so I'd expect a fair day rather than a hot one.
- St. Joseph's July 10 report was excellent, but its July 3 report was poor. That swing is why I'd keep it as the backup rather than the first choice.
- I'd expect a cold-water drop (upwelling) to help. Past Augusts with a sharp surface-temperature drop had good boat reports at several ports (Muskegon, South Haven, Grand Haven, 2023), so a drop would be the reason to switch to St. Joseph.

## Evidence
**Recent reports**
- Grand Haven, July 24: Chinook and coho boat fishing "35 to 100 down in 60 to 120 feet of water"; "Green and orange spoons worked well along with white flasher flies." Chinook unrated, coho quality 1 (Grand Haven, 2024-07-24).
- Grand Haven, July 10: boat quality 2 for Chinook and coho, best at "40 to 100 down in 65 to 120 feet of water," with meat rigs and orange spoons (Grand Haven, 2024-07-10).
- Muskegon, July 10: boat quality 2, "40 to 100 feet down in 70 to 120 feet of water," with meat rigs and flashers (Muskegon, 2024-07-10).
- South Haven, July 10: boat quality 2, mixed coho and Chinook; best at "75 to 80 feet" and "105 to 110 feet" of water; rotators and flies worked (South Haven, 2024-07-10).
- St. Joseph, July 10: boat quality 4, "The most productive depths were 80 to 90 feet of water," mostly on spoons (St. Joseph, 2024-07-10).
- St. Joseph, July 3: only "a few coho salmon and steelhead," best near 100 ft; quality 1 (St. Joseph, 2024-07-03).

**Past seasons (history, not this week)**
- In late July and August with surface water near 70 F, boat reports across these ports ranged from 0 to 3, and most were 2 or 3.
- The August 2023 reports after a sharp surface drop were good at Muskegon, South Haven and Grand Haven (quality 3). The August 2022 Grand Haven report after a drop was 2 (Grand Haven, 2023-08-16; Muskegon, 2023-08-16; South Haven, 2023-08-16; Grand Haven, 2022-08-17).

**Conditions**
- The conditions tool returned a summary for the week before July 30, not live readings. Buoy surface water was 73 F at St. Joseph, 71 F at South Haven, and 68 F at Grand Haven and Muskegon, with 1-2 F of change over the week (conditions summary, week before 2024-07-30).
- General guidance (NY DEC): Chinook and coho prefer 52-58 F, so at these surface temperatures the fish are likely deeper, near the cold layer. This is general guidance, not something a report said.

## Caveats
- The newest report is 6 days old (Grand Haven, July 24). The St. Joseph, South Haven and Muskegon reports are 20 days old (July 10), so this week's ratings are estimates.
- The conditions I got are a backtest summary from the week before July 30, not live buoy or wind data. I couldn't check this week's wind, so check the forecast before you go.
- Surface readings of 68-73 F are above the 52-58 F range for Chinook and coho, so depth is the main thing to adjust.

## Sources
- Grand Haven, July 24: https://content.govdelivery.com/accounts/MIDNR/bulletins/3aa7f0e
